paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD is in charge of everything, and He is in charge of YOU. He says, "I am the LORD, and there is no other." (Isaiah 45:5) He stretched out the heavens by Himself, and He says He does all these things (Isaiah 44:24; 45:7). So when life gets loud and confusing, the One holding it all is not confused.

Now look at Cyrus, king of Persia. The LORD calls him by name and says He will equip him "though you have not known Me." (Isaiah 45:4-5) Cyrus did not have to know the LORD first for the LORD to be at work, and the LORD says He does it so that all may know there is none but Him (Isaiah 45:6). I think that should make a baker feel two things at once: small, because the work belongs to God, and safe, because the work is in good hands.

That brings us to the clay and the potter. "Does the clay ask the potter, 'What are you making?'" (Isaiah 45:9) I know I want the full blueprint before I say yes to anything, but the LORD is asking for trust instead. The One who made the earth and the people on it can be trusted with the plan, and He keeps His word to His people: Cyrus will rebuild His city and set His exiles free (Isaiah 45:13). The story isn't over, and the LORD is still the One who calls and keeps.
